items.title: Checking the rule of 72
items.prose: At 9% a year the rule of 72 predicts doubling in $72 \div 9 = 8$ years.
items.question: What is $1.09^8$, to two decimal places?

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Multiply 1.09 by itself 8 times.

byKey.simple: You added 9% eight times: $1 + 8 \times 0.09$. Compounding multiplies by 1.09 eight times.
byKey.exact: The rule is an estimate. Work out $1.09^8$ itself; it is just under 2.

explain.text: $1.09^8 \approx 1.9926$. So 8 years at 9% almost exactly doubles money, as the rule of 72 predicts.

items.title: Why compounding pulls ahead

items.title: Twenty years at 5%
items.prompt:
You invest £5,000.00 at 5% a year, compounded yearly, for 20 years.

(a) Write the balance $V_n$ after $n$ years as a rule.

(b) Compute the balance after 10 years and after 20 years, to the penny.

(c) Compute the balance after 20 years with simple interest of 5% of £5,000.00 a year. Explain the difference.

(d) Use the rule of 72 to estimate the doubling time. Check it with your rule from (a).

(e) Use the index laws to explain why the doubling time depends on neither the start nor the year.
items.model:
**(a)** Each year multiplies the balance by $1 + 0.05 = 1.05$. After $n$ years, $V_n = 5000 \times 1.05^n$.

**(b)** $V_{10} = 5000 \times 1.05^{10} \approx 5000 \times 1.6288946 = 8144.47$, so £8,144.47. $V_{20} = 5000 \times 1.05^{20} \approx 5000 \times 2.6532977 = 13266.49$, so £13,266.49.

**(c)** Simple interest adds 5% of £5,000.00, which is £250.00, each year. After 20 years that gives $5000 + 20 \times 250 = 10000$, so £10,000.00. Compounding is ahead by £3,266.49, because each year's 5% is also earned on earlier interest.

**(d)** The rule of 72 gives $72 \div 5 = 14.4$ years. Check: $V_{14} = 5000 \times 1.05^{14} \approx 9899.66$ and $V_{15} = 5000 \times 1.05^{15} \approx 10394.64$. The balance passes £10,000.00 between years 14 and 15, so the estimate is good.

**(e)** Over any $h$ years, $\dfrac{V_{n+h}}{V_n} = \dfrac{5000 \times 1.05^{n+h}}{5000 \times 1.05^n} = 1.05^h$, by the index laws. The £5,000.00 cancels and so does $n$. The doubling time is the $h$ with $1.05^h = 2$, which is the same for any start and any year.

rubric.text: Writes $V_n = 5000 \times 1.05^n$, with the factor 1.05 explained as $1 + 0.05$.
Gives £8,144.47 after 10 years and £13,266.49 after 20 years.
Gives £10,000.00 for simple interest and explains the £3,266.49 gap as interest earned on interest.
Estimates 14.4 years and checks that the balance passes £10,000.00 between years 14 and 15.
Shows $V_{n+h} / V_n = 1.05^h$, so the start and $n$ cancel, and names the doubling time as the $h$ with $1.05^h = 2$.
